raw_segments.text: Public stock and public lands, therefore, the two sources of revenue which may peculiarly
belong to the sovereign or commonwealth, being both improper and insufficient funds for defraying
the necessary expense of any great and civilized state.
It remains that this expense must, the greater part of it, be defrayed by taxes of one kind
or another, the people contributing a part of their own private revenue, in order to
make up a public revenue to the sovereign or commonwealth.
